raw_case_text:
A 28-year-old female patient presented to the emergency department of our hospital with a 4-week history of fever, loss of appetite, and myalgia, followed by the onset of skin lesions.
The lesions first began on the trunk and gradually involved the face and the extremities. She also gave a history of weight loss over the past 6 months. She is married with two children, but the husband has been estranged for the past 1 year.
The patient did not give a history of any genital lesion in the past.
The physical examination revealed that the patient was afebrile, conscious, and well-oriented to time, place, and person. She was severely underweight with a BMI of 16.33 (weight -36 kg and height -1.49 m).
There was no pallor/icterus/cyanosis; a few enlarged lymph nodes were seen in the bilateral inguinal region; peripheral edema was present over the bilateral lower limbs extending up to the knee.
The cutaneous examination revealed multiple nodules over the face, the trunk, and the upper and lower limbs. The nodules were covered with thick, yellowish, rupioid-like crusts, and some of them were ulcerated. There was mutilation of the nasal tip, and scarring was present wherever the necrotic crusts were present [Figure 1a-c].
On examination of the oral mucosa, thrush was seen on the tongue and over the buccal mucosa. The genital mucosa appeared normal. There were lesions over the eyelids; however, the ophthalmological examination revealed no significant abnormality.
The neurological, gastrointestinal tract, musculoskeletal, and cardiovascular examinations were all within the normal limits.
From the cutaneous presentation, a differential diagnosis of pemphigus vegetans, pyoderma gangrenosum, lupus vulgaris, deep fungal infection, rupioid psoriasis, and secondary syphilis was thought of.
The patient was admitted and investigated further.
The serum investigations revealed a positive Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR) (TITER-1:4) and a positive Treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay status. After further enquiry, the patient revealed that she had been diagnosed as HIV positive in the past 6 months, had been started on antiretroviral treatment, but had not continued taking the treatment.
A CD4 cell count was 90 cells/mm3. The serology for hepatitis B and C was negative. A complete blood count revealed pancytopenia with a total white blood cell count of 21,000 and hemoglobin -7.7 gm%, and the liver function test revealed a serum albumin of 2.2 gm% with a total protein level of 6.6. The Mantoux test was negative.
A histopathological examination of the skin revealed pustule formation, i.e. neutrophil collection in the stratum corneum, ulceration, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, inflammatory cells consisting of plasma cells, and histiocytes was seen in the dermis [Figure 2a-c].
Stains for fungal elements were negative. The Ziehl-Neelsen stain was negative. No granulomas or clefting were seen.
Considering the VDRL positivity, HIV positivity, and histopathology revealing plasma cells, a diagnosis of MS was made.
The patient was treated with 2.4 million units of benzathine penicillin in a total of three series with an interval of 1 week between the series. The patient showed a significant improvement after each dose [Figures 3-5]. Owing to the low CD4 counts - cotrimoxazole (800/160) and fluconazole (100 mg) prophylaxis was also started. Antiretroviral therapy was started after the completion of the course of benzathine penicillin in view of preventing immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome). The lesions healed completely with scarring.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old female presented with a 4-week history of fever, anorexia, and myalgia followed by widespread ulcerated crusted nodular skin lesions.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced 4 weeks of fever, loss of appetite, and myalgia, followed by the eruption of nodular skin lesions that began on the trunk and progressively spread to her face and upper and lower extremities, accompanied by significant weight loss over the preceding 6 months.
subjective.past_medical_history: Married with two children, estranged from her husband for the past 1 year. Upon further inquiry after admission, she disclosed having been diagnosed with HIV infection 6 months earlier and initiated on antiretroviral therapy (ART), which she subsequently discontinued. Denied any history of prior genital lesions.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, anorexia, myalgia, 6-month weight loss, and widespread crusted skin nodules. Discontinued home ART.

objective.physical_examination: The patient was afebrile, conscious, and oriented, but severely underweight (weight 36 kg, height 1.49 m, BMI 16.33 kg/m2) without pallor, icterus, or cyanosis. Examination revealed bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy and bilateral pitting lower-limb edema extending to the knees. Cutaneous examination showed widespread nodules over the face, eyelids, trunk, and extremities covered by thick, yellowish rupioid-like necrotic crusts with underlying ulceration, scarring, and mutilation of the nasal tip. Oral mucosa showed candidal thrush on the tongue and buccal mucosa; genital mucosa, ophthalmic exam, and cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, musculoskeletal, and neurological exams were normal.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC showed hemoglobin 7.7 g/dL and leukocytosis with total WBC count 21,000/mm3 (reported alongside pancytopenia/anemia). Liver function tests revealed hypoalbuminemia (albumin 2.2 g/dL) with total protein 6.6 g/dL. Hepatitis B and C serologies and Mantoux tuberculin skin test were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4 T-lymphocyte count was severely depressed at 90 cells/mm3. Skin biopsy histopathology demonstrated stratum corneum pustule formation (neutrophilic collections), epidermal ulceration, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, and a dense dermal inflammatory infiltrate composed of plasma cells and histiocytes; fungal (PAS/GMS) and Ziehl-Neelsen acid-fast stains were negative, with no granulomas or acantholytic clefting.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed malignant syphilis (lues maligna) co-infected with advanced HIV (CD4 90 cells/mm3) and oral candidiasis, established via reactive serum VDRL/RPR (titer 1:4), positive TPHA, and characteristic plasma-cell-rich dermal histopathology (ruling out pemphigus vegetans, pyoderma gangrenosum, lupus vulgaris, deep mycosis, and rupioid psoriasis). Treated with intramuscular benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units once weekly for 3 doses, plus cotrimoxazole (800/160 mg) and fluconazole (100 mg) prophylaxis, followed by re-initiation of antiretroviral therapy after completing penicillin to minimize IRIS risk. The cutaneous lesions healed completely with residual scarring.
